title: Yellowed Crispy Japanese Bamboo Shoot Tsukune
description: A traditional Japanese dish from the Shikoku region, featuring crispy bamboo shoots in a tsukune form, with a bitter and cozy flavor profile, this low-carb-friendly recipe is perfect for a snack or dinner

ingredients.name: Bamboo shoots
ingredients.notes: canned or fresh, sliced into 1/4 inch thick rounds

instructions: In a large bowl, mix together salt and water to create a brine, stirring until the salt is dissolved.
Add the sliced bamboo shoots to the brine and let it sit for at least 2 hours or overnight in the refrigerator.
Preheat the oven to 400 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a separate bowl, mix together rice flour, grated daikon, sesame oil, soy sauce, sugar, and black pepper.
Remove the bamboo shoots from the brine and pat them dry with paper towels.
Add the beaten egg to the rice flour mixture and stir until it forms a sticky dough.
Add the bamboo shoots to the dough and mix until they are well coated.
Use your hands to shape the mixture into small tsukune forms, about 1 1/2 inches in diameter and 1/2 inch thick.
Place the tsukune on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and bake for 20 minutes, flipping them halfway through.
Increase the oven temperature to broil and cook for an additional 2-3 minutes, or until the tsukune are crispy and golden brown.
